candidate_findings.message: Under StrictMode, every delete in the running app may log two 'removed' activity entries, because deleteItem queues a state update from inside another state updater; the new delete-activity test cannot catch this. deleteItem calls `setActivities(prevAct => [activity, ...prevAct])` inside the `setItems(prev => {...})` updater. src/main.tsx wraps <App /> in <StrictMode>, and React runs updater functions twice in development. The new test 'adds activity when deleting an item' uses renderHook without StrictMode, so it checks only the single-invocation case.

Editing an item through the new Edit flow writes no activity entry, so the Recent Activity feed shows adds and deletes but never edits. updateItem only calls setItems and never calls setActivities. addItem (line 38) and deleteItem (line 74) both log activity, and ActivityEntry.action in src/types/inventory.ts already includes 'updated'. The diff wires updateItem to the new Edit button (App.tsx `onUpdate={updateItem}`) without adding a log entry, and no test covers edit activity.

None of the new edit UI has a test: the Edit button, the modal's edit pre-fill, the 'Save Changes' submit path and the remount-by-key reset could all break without any test failing. The only test the diff adds is a hook test for deleteItem activity. No test renders InventoryTable's new `onEdit` button, AddItemModal with `editItem`/`onUpdate`, or InventoryPage's `openModal(item)` and `modalKey` logic.

The added test cannot fail on the baseline, because the change does not touch the behaviour it checks, so it adds no evidence for this change. The diff does not modify src/hooks/useInventory.ts. deleteItem's 'removed' activity logging (lines 57-78) already exists, so 'adds activity when deleting an item' passes before and after the change.

If the modal is ever given editItem without onUpdate, Save silently creates a duplicate item instead of failing, because onUpdate is optional and the code falls back to onAdd. `if (isEditMode && editItem && onUpdate) { onUpdate(editItem.id, form) } else { onAdd(form) }`, with `onUpdate?:` optional in AddItemModalProps. InventoryPage always passes onUpdate today, so the current app does not hit this path.

The component is still named AddItemModal but now handles both add and edit, and the README still describes it only as the 'add item modal'. `export default function AddItemModal({ isOpen, onClose, onAdd, editItem, onUpdate })` switches its heading and button text on `isEditMode`. README.md line 39 reads 'Inventory table, add item modal, status badges'.

The new Edit button sits directly beside a Delete button that removes the item in one click with no confirmation or undo, which makes an accidental, unrecoverable delete more likely. The diff inserts the Edit button (`className="mr-1 ..."`) right before `<button onClick={() => onDelete(item.id)}`. deleteItem filters the item out of state immediately, and there is no confirm step or restore path.

ADDITIONAL_HF_REPOS is now a required config key, so an existing catalog whose config.yaml lacks it (or has one malformed entry) now fails config validation as a whole, and the site falls back to empty defaults and shows no catalog at all. main.js:765-766 pushes 'ADDITIONAL_HF_REPOS (must be a list)' when the key is absent, and lines 769-774 do the same for any bad entry. Line 782 then throws, and the catch at 792-799 replaces the whole CONFIG with ORGANIZATION_NAME: ''. The guard at main.js:897 ('if (!ORGANIZATION_NAME) return;') then stops the data loading. Before this change, a config without the key loaded normally. This repo is a template ('Welcome to your new catalog repo', README), so downstream catalogs that pick up the new main.js without editing their config.yaml hit this. Treating a missing key as [] would keep them working.

export-tags.js now throws for any config.yaml that lacks ADDITIONAL_HF_REPOS, so the dev script stops working on existing configs even though the feature is optional. export-tags.js:48-52 says 'if (!Array.isArray(CONFIG.ADDITIONAL_HF_REPOS)) throw new Error(...)'. The requiredKeys list at line 32 and the header comment at line 11 don't mention the new key, so the script's documented contract and its behaviour disagree.

Two config entries that name the same HF repo with different letter case are both fetched and both added, so the same repo can appear twice in the catalog. Deduplication at main.js:304-308 compares the raw entry.repo strings ('seenRepos.has(entry.repo)'), and line 326 filters only against existingIds, which holds the org listing alone. Hugging Face resolves repo paths case-insensitively and returns the canonical id. So 'User/x' and 'user/x' both get past seenRepos, both come back with id 'user/x', and both are appended. The same logic is in scripts/export-tags.js:127-139.

Each additional model is fetched from the same endpoint twice per page load: once in the new block, then again in the existing per-model detail step. The new code fetches `${API_BASE_URL}${repoType}/${entry.repo}` (line 312), which for models is `${API_BASE_URL}models/<id>`. It appends the result to hfItems, and the existing Step 2 at line 332 then fetches `${API_BASE_URL}models/${item.id}` for every item in hfItems, including those just fetched.

No tests cover the new behaviour: merging extra repos per type, skipping duplicates, tolerating failed fetches, and validating config entries. The diff touches only README.md, main.js, public/config.yaml and scripts/export-tags.js. A glob for *.test.* / *.spec.* in the export finds no test files, so none of the new branches (main.js:300-327 and 765-775) is checked by anything automated.

In the tag-export script, a failed fetch of an additional HF repo is dropped silently, so a typo in a repo name leaves its tags out of tag-export.txt with no warning. export-tags.js:134-136 uses `get(...).then(({ json }) => json).catch(() => null)` with no logging. The browser version at main.js:315 and 321 calls console.warn for the same failure.

The new validation message puts JSON.stringify of config entries into the error banner, which is rendered with innerHTML, so markup in a config value is interpreted as HTML. Line 773 adds `bad entries: ${badEntries.map(e => JSON.stringify(e)).join(', ')}` to the message. main.js:788 renders it with `errorDiv.innerHTML = `Configuration Error: ${error.message}...``. The input is owner-controlled config, so impact is limited.

entry.repo goes into the API URL unencoded and is only checked for being a non-empty string, so a value with '?', '#' or '../' would request a different API path than intended. main.js:312 builds `${API_BASE_URL}${repoType}/${entry.repo}`, and validation at line 770 checks only `typeof e.repo !== 'string' || !e.repo.trim()`, with no owner/name format check. The value comes from the site owner's config, so the risk is low. The same applies to scripts/export-tags.js:134.

The validation rules and the fetch-and-merge logic for additional HF repos are copied between main.js and scripts/export-tags.js, so the two can drift apart, and already differ in how they log errors. export-tags.js:53-61 repeats main.js:768-774 nearly word for word, and export-tags.js:123-140 repeats main.js:300-327.

The change removes `defmt` from the crate's default features. Nothing in the packet asks for this, and downstream users who rely on the default `defmt::Format` impl on `Error` will stop compiling or lose logging support without warning. The diff changes `default = ["esa", "bdd", "macros", "defmt"]` to `default = ["esa", "bdd", "macros"]`. In lib.rs:158, `#[cfg_attr(feature = "defmt", derive(defmt::Format))]` on `pub enum Error<E>` is now off by default. The rest of the diff only adds the PartitionGuard lock/try_lock API and overflow checks, none of which needs this public default to change.

The change adds a new dev-dependency, `critical-section` with the `std` feature, that nothing in the crate visibly uses. It may be unneeded supply-chain surface, and no reason for it is given. `critical-section = { workspace = true, features = ["std"] }` is added under [dev-dependencies], and Cargo.lock gains a `critical-section` entry for partition-manager. A search of partition-manager/ for `critical_section` or `CriticalSection` finds nothing. The tests build `TestMap` with `NoopRawMutex` (test/mod.rs:16-24).

PartitionGuard copies the bounds-checking logic of Partition (`start_block`, `check_access`, and `within_bounds` in lib.rs) instead of sharing it, so a later fix to one copy can silently miss the other. In bdd.rs, `impl PartitionGuard { const fn start_block ...; const fn check_access ... }` repeats the Partition versions line for line: the checked_mul, the `data.len() > u32::MAX` test, and the within_bounds call. lib.rs:138-148 duplicates `within_bounds` from lib.rs:126-136. In esa.rs, the guard's read/write/erase bodies (lines ~265-312) repeat the Partition bodies except that they call `self.guard` instead of `self.storage.lock().await`.

Holding a PartitionGuard blocks every other partition on the same device, because they all share one mutex. If a task awaits any Partition operation (or `lock()` on another partition) while holding a guard, it waits forever, and neither the docs nor the README warn about this. `lock()` returns a guard that holds `self.storage.lock().await`. Every partition shares that `&Mutex<M, F>` (test/mod.rs map). The test at test/bdd.rs:128-132 confirms that holding `factory.lock()` makes `settings.try_lock()` fail. The doc comment only says 'The underlying mutex is held for the lifetime of this guard'. README.md:76 describes the Mutex but not the new lock API.

The new tests leave some guard paths untested: the RO guard's `write` returning `ReadOnly`, guard erase going out of bounds or with `to < from`, and guard writes just past the partition end. A wrong bounds or read-only check on those guard impls would still pass. The only negative guard checks are `guard.read(u32::MAX, ...)` (bdd.rs:125) and `guard.write(0x1000, &[0xFE, 0xFD])` (esa.rs test). No test obtains a guard on a `Partition<_, RO, _>`, for example via `readonly().lock()`, and no test calls `erase` on a guard with bad bounds.

The `EEXIST + --push` retry path never checks that the current plan file still matches the marker's sha256, so it can publish an edited, never-approved plan to the board as the 'approved plan'. Lines 390-394: on EEXIST with `--push`, the marker is 'not re-written', Step 4b is skipped and the flow goes 'directly to Step 4c'. Step 4c then reads `.clancy/plans/{stem}.md` (line 504) and posts its content through the curl blocks. Nothing in 4a's retry branch or in 4c hashes the plan and compares it to the marker's `sha256=`, even though lines 410-412 describe that comparison as the gate. Trigger: approve plan X, the push fails, edit X.md, then run the printed retry command `/clancy:approve-plan X --push --ticket KEY`. The edited content is posted to the ticket while the marker still holds the old hash. The same branch also re-posts a duplicate comment when the earlier push succeeded, because it never checks for a prior `LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN_PUSH` row.

The bracketed-key Source parser cannot match Notion keys (hex/UUID) or Shortcut-style keys, so Notion auto-detect never pushes and Notion Sources are wrongly classed as 'file-path'. The pushable pattern is `^\[(#?\d+|[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-\d+)\]\s+.+$`, which allows only `#digits`, bare digits or `UPPER-digits`. Brief writes board Sources as `[{KEY}] {Title}` (brief.md:808), and Notion keys are `^[0-9a-f]{32}$|^[0-9a-f-]{36}$` (line 186 table). So `[3f2a…] Title` falls into bucket 3 ('matches anything else', line 526). That logs `BOARD_PUSH_SKIPPED_NO_TICKET | file-path` and shows 'source is file-path', which is wrong. The Notion success note added to Step 7 (line 1504) can then only fire through `--ticket`. Shortcut's `[SC-123]`, which Step 2 line 106 accepts, parses as bracketed but then hard-errors against `^\d+$`.

The `--ticket` override is never honoured when the plan has no Source header or has an inline-quoted or file-path Source, because those branches skip before the override is considered. This contradicts the command doc's promise that `--ticket` helps when Source is 'missing'. Line 518 says a missing `**Source:**` header makes Step 4c 'skip silently and continue to Step 7', with no `--ticket` exception. The skip-no-ticket branch (lines 530-546) logs `BOARD_PUSH_SKIPPED_NO_TICKET` and continues to Step 7, again with no exception. `--ticket` is first mentioned at line 550, after both exits. The diff's commands/approve-plan.md says `--ticket` is 'Useful when the brief Source field is missing, ambiguous'. Trigger: `/clancy:approve-plan foo --push --ticket PROJ-1` on a plan whose Source is `"Add dark mode"` follows the documented order to the skip branch, and nothing is pushed.

Step 2 still says the board push for plan-file stems is deferred and that the marker is the only side effect. This contradicts the new Step 4c, so the LLM running the workflow gets conflicting instructions about whether to push. Line 98: 'The board push offer for plan-file-stem mode is deferred to a future PR — for now the local marker is the only side effect.' The diff updated the Overview (line 8) and the 4a/4b tails to route into Step 4c, but left this sentence unchanged.

The success and failure classification depends on the HTTP status, but the duplicated curl commands never capture one. A 4xx/5xx response may be logged as a successful push. Every push block uses `curl -s` without `--fail` or `-w '%{http_code}'` (e.g. lines 638-646 and 662-668). With those options absent, curl exits 0 on HTTP 401/403/500. Yet line 742 keys success on 'When the curl returns a 2xx response' and logs `LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN_PUSH`, and lines 760-762 require 'the literal numeric status code' for `BOARD_PUSH_FAILED`. Nothing in the commands provides that code.

The plan body and identifiers are placed inside single-quoted `-d '...'` shell arguments. Plan text containing a `'` can break out into the shell, and `$ISSUE_ID`/`$PAGE_ID` never expand. The new `--afk --push` path reaches this sink unattended. Line 681: `-d '{"query": "mutation { commentCreate(input: { issueId: \"$ISSUE_ID\", body: \"<markdown plan>\" }) ...'`. Line 731: `-d '{"parent": {"page_id": "$PAGE_ID"}, ...}'`. Inside single quotes `$ISSUE_ID`/`$PAGE_ID` stay literal. The `<markdown plan>` content comes from the plan file, which derives from briefs and board tickets, and is interpolated with no encoding or escaping rule. Step 4c also never says how `{KEY}` maps to `$ISSUE_NUMBER` (strip `#`), `$ISSUE_ID` or `$PAGE_ID`. These blocks were copied from plan.md Step 5b, but this change adds an unattended path to them.

The `--afk`-without-`--push` decision is placed after Source parsing and key validation. An unattended run that is meant to stay local-only can therefore print a hard error and log `BOARD_PUSH_FAILED` or `BOARD_PUSH_SKIPPED_NO_TICKET` alongside or instead of `LOCAL_ONLY`. The documented order in Step 4c is: read Source (502) → parse and skip-no-ticket logging (520-546) → validate and hard-error, logging `BOARD_PUSH_FAILED | key-mismatch:{KEY}` (548-589) → decision matrix (608-627), where '`--afk` without `--push`' should 'Skip the push entirely'. No sentence moves the flag check ahead of the parse and validate sub-steps, so a mismatched Source key under plain `--afk` follows the hard-error path first.

The retry path claims auditors 'see one approval row', but Step 7 unconditionally re-renders '✅ Approved' and appends another `LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN` row on every `--push` retry. Line 396: 'auditing tools see one approval row in `.clancy/progress.txt`, even if 4c was attempted multiple times.' Step 7 local mode (lines 1478-1516) always prints the approved block and 'Append to `.clancy/progress.txt`: ... LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN | sha256=...' with no retry exception. Line 493's gate also still reads 'Step 4a wrote a marker successfully', which is false on the retry path.

The diff rewrites an existing locked baseline test's expectation in the same change it judges. The baseline test `after writing the marker, Step 4a jumps to Step 7 (log) and skips board flow` asserted `content.toContain('jump to Step 7')`. The diff replaces it with `continues to Step 4c` assertions. The behaviour change is intended, but acceptance.md says the baseline tests are locked, and the edit carries no recorded approval.

The new tests only regex-match prose shape, and some are tautological, so they would pass with a wrong or contradictory workflow (for example, none catches the stale Step 2 'deferred' sentence or the --ticket ordering bug). 'command file --push doc references board push target' slices from the index of '`--push`' and then asserts `/push|board/i`, which the slice always matches because it begins with `--push`. 'documents the three brief Source formats' accepts `/file[- ]path|\.md/`, and `.md` appears throughout. Every Step 4c test is a `toMatch` on markdown text, and none exercises behaviour.

The migration also switches the primary keys of all three tables from AutoField to BigAutoField. The story didn't ask for this, and on a large RateLimitEntry table it may rewrite and lock the table during `migrate`, which would block rate-limited requests. Lines 286-306 add `migrations.AlterField(... name="id", field=models.BigAutoField(...))` for ratelimitconfig, ratelimitcounter and ratelimitentry. 0001_initial.py creates those ids as `models.AutoField`. The change only needed the `AddField` for `data`. The ALTER is there because the migration was generated by makemigrations (header: 'Generated by Django 5.2.1') against apps.py `default_auto_field = "django.db.models.BigAutoField"`, which is unrelated to the bug.

The index renames run only when the installed Django has `RenameIndex`. Installs on Django 3.2 or 4.0, which the project still supports, end up with a different migration state and different database index names. On those versions the model's indexes no longer match migration state, so `makemigrations` would generate a new migration inside the installed package, and any later migration that relies on the new names will break. Line 232 has `RenameIndex = getattr(migrations, "RenameIndex", None)`, and line 243 has `if RenameIndex is not None: rename_operations.extend([...])`. pyproject.toml lists 'Framework :: Django :: 3.2' and '4.0' and requires `Django>=3.2`. The model Meta indexes in models.py are unnamed, so Django derives the new names, which differ from the names in 0001_initial (for example `django_smar_key_24c4a0_idx`).

The diff adds no test that database token buckets keep their state across requests. That is the behaviour the change exists to fix, yet the committed checklist marks 'Add or update automated tests' as done. Because the database errors are caught, a regression here would silently let every request through. diff.patch touches no file under tests/. tests/backends/test_database_backend.py has no `token_bucket_check` test, and tests/algorithms/test_token_bucket.py never refers to DatabaseBackend. CHECKLIST_database_backend_fix.md line 15 says `- [x] Add or update automated tests (unit/integration) that expose the bug and verify the fix.` The `except Exception` handler in `token_bucket_check` (lines 205-219) returns `True` (allowed) on any error, including a missing `data` column.

`get()` now runs stored values back through JSON parsing, so the type can change between `set()` and `get()`. For example, `set(k, "123")` reads back as int 123 and `set(k, "true")` reads back as bool True. `set()` stores `serialize_data(value)`, which returns `str(data)` for str, int and float. `get()` returns `deserialize_data(counter.data)`, and with no expected_type that is `json.loads(data)`. Any string that is valid JSON therefore comes back as a different type.

The migration has no tested rollback that keeps data. Reversing it drops the new `data` column and every serialized token-bucket state and `set()` value with it. Reversing BigAutoField to AutoField may fail once ids pass 2^31. The diff has no rollback rehearsal and no declared breaking-change path. The operations are a plain `AddField` (its reverse is RemoveField, so the column contents are lost) and `AlterField` to BigAutoField (its reverse narrows to int). There is no `RunPython` or state-preserving reverse, and the diff adds no test of the migration in either direction. The risk.json review focus asks: 'does the down path restore data, not just schema; is the rollback rehearsed?'

The change commits a working checklist to the repository root. It is unrelated to the story and contains a developer's absolute local paths. Its ticked boxes claim verification work that the diff doesn't show. This is a new file. It contains `/Users/<author>/Documents/GitHub/django-ratelimit-base/django-test-project` and `/Users/<author>/Documents/GitHub/django-test-project`, and every item is marked `[x]`, including running `make ci-check` and re-running the scenario.

`token_bucket_check` and `token_bucket_info` contain the same block for parsing stored bucket state, so a fix to one can easily miss the other. Lines 117-126 and 242-249 repeat the same sequence: `deserialize_data(counter.data, dict) if counter.data else {}`, the isinstance-dict guard, `float(bucket_data.get("tokens", counter.count))` and `float(bucket_data.get("last_refill", counter.updated_at.timestamp()))`. The two copies are not in a shared helper.

The new doc lines say `showmigrations` verifies that the `data` column exists. It only lists which migrations are recorded as applied and never inspects columns. backends.md also says 'Starting with the next release' instead of giving a version. installation.md adds `# Optional: verify that the RateLimitCounter table now includes the `data` column` followed by `python manage.py showmigrations django_smart_ratelimit`, and the same pairing appears again at line 265. docs/backends.md adds '> **Note:** Starting with the next release, `RateLimitCounter` includes a `data` column'. docs/design.md picks up a stray blank line at line 158.

Launching ".NET API: Debug" on its own (root launch.json or backend workspace) stops the Docker exp container and starts nothing on port 5002, so the API it launches cannot fetch its startup config from EXP_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:5002. launch.json:62 sets preLaunchTask "Build: API for Debug". In tasks.json that task has dependsOn ["Infra: Setup Docker"], which runs `npm run dev:local:setup` → scripts/dev-local.ts --setup-only. main() always calls swapExpToBareMetalMode(), which runs `docker stop exp-arolariu-ro`, and BARE_METAL_SERVICES["setup-only"] is []. The config itself sets EXP_PROXY_URL to http://localhost:5002, and AddProxyConfiguration fetches Auth:JWT:Secret and the other keys at startup. Only the compound also starts exp. DEVELOPMENT.md still lists ".NET API: Debug" as a standalone profile.

Each orchestrator run starts the Docker exp container again with `docker compose up -d` before stopping it. In the Full Stack compound the bare-metal exp launches at the same time as this preLaunchTask, so both may race for host port 5002 and either uvicorn or the compose step can fail. startStorage() runs `docker compose -f Storage/docker-compose.yml up -d`. That compose file defines service exp (container exp-arolariu-ro, ports "5002:80", with a build section), so it is started or built on every run. swapExpToBareMetalMode() stops it only afterwards. In the compounds (launch.json "Full Stack: Website + API + exp" and fullstack.code-workspace), "Python: exp FastAPI Debug" has no preLaunchTask and binds 127.0.0.1:5002 while the API's preLaunchTask is still running this sequence. If dockerCompose() throws, main() exits 1 and the API debug session never starts.

The Azurite readiness probe may never return a 2xx response, because it sends an unauthenticated account-level list request. Every `dev:local` run and every debug preLaunchTask would then wait the full 60s timeout, which contradicts the documented ~3-second preLaunchTask. waitForHealth("http://localhost:10000/devstoreaccount1?comp=list", ...) treats only `response.ok` as healthy and sends no Authorization or SAS. Azurite runs with `--oauth basic`, and an anonymous account-level List Containers call is rejected unless public access applies. The compose healthcheck for Azurite uses only a TCP connect. DEVELOPMENT.md says: "If Docker infra is already running, the preLaunchTask completes in ~3 seconds."

The Azurite init swallows every error inside the child script, so the orchestrator reports "Azurite blob containers initialized with CORS" even when container creation or the CORS setup failed. The `node -e` script ends with `.catch(()=>{})`, so the child always exits 0. The surrounding try/catch therefore never reaches logWarning, and logSuccess runs unconditionally. The original selfhost-start.sh at least printed `e.message`.

The new script hardcodes the MSSQL SA password and the Azurite account key in source, adding another copy of the credential to keep in sync. Line 145 runs `sqlcmd ... -U sa -P "qazWSXedcRFV1234!"` and the Azurite connection string embeds AccountKey=Eby8vdM02x.... These are local-emulator values that already appear in infra/Local/Storage/docker-comp.yml (MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD) and in selfhost-start.sh. selfhost-start.sh reads the password from $MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD, while this script uses a literal.

Whether Entra ID auth is used now depends on an exact string match of the URL rather than on the Azure identity. An EXP_PROXY_URL such as "https://exp.arolariu.ro/" (trailing slash) or any other Azure-hosted exp URL silently drops the bearer token. The .NET side, which does not trim, behaves differently from the TS side, which does. configProxy.ts: `const USE_AZURE_AUTH = EXP_BASE_URL === AZURE_EXP_URL;` after `process.env["EXP_PROXY_URL"]?.trim() || ...`. generate.env.ts has the same logic. WebApplicationBuilderExtensions.cs:122: `var useAzureAuth = baseUrl == ConfigProxyUrlAzure;` with `explicitUrl` taken untrimmed from Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable. Before this change, auth was keyed on AZURE_CLIENT_ID being present.

Placing the new "Development" profile first makes it the default for `dotnet run`/`dotnet watch run`. Every default local launch therefore now forces EXP_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:5002 and HTTP on :5000, replacing the previous "Console App" default (HTTPS, no exp override). "Development" is inserted before "Console App" in profiles, and the dotnet CLI uses the first Project profile when --launch-profile is absent. Its environmentVariables set EXP_PROXY_URL and INFRA, so any developer whose exp runs only in Docker (http://exp) now gets an API pointed at localhost:5002.

The new exp test and lint targets pip-install into whatever Python interpreter is active, with no virtualenv, on every run. Because the root `npm run test` / `test:unit` use `run-many --all`, these targets may now run in workflows that never set up Python. The test target command is `python -m pip install -q -r requirements-dev.txt && python -m pytest -q` (lint is similar). The root package.json has "test": "nx run-many --target=test --all" and "test:unit": "nx run-many --target=test --configuration=unit --all". .github/scripts/src/hygiene/checks/testCheck.ts runs `npm run test:unit`. The exp target defines no `unit` configuration. The new pinned dev dependencies (pytest==9.0.2, ruff==0.15.4) are installed this way.

The script's own usage docs and one branch disagree with what it does: --frontend and --infra also start exp, and the "Infrastructure-only mode" branch can never run. The header says `--frontend  # Start infra + website only` and `--infra  # Start infra only (no services)`. However, BARE_METAL_SERVICES has frontend: ["exp","website"] and infra: ["exp"]. `if (bareMetalServices.length === 0)` is true only for "setup-only", so the else branch that prints "Infrastructure-only mode. Start services manually" is dead code. Step 2 also logs "Starting databases (... exp)" just before the script stops exp.

The new endpoint and auth selection logic, which decides whether config requests carry a bearer token, ships without any test in the .NET API, the website or generate.env.ts. The diff changes the baseUrl and useAzureAuth logic in AddProxyConfiguration, and EXP_BASE_URL/USE_AZURE_AUTH in configProxy.ts and generate.env.ts. It adds no test file: the only test-related additions are the exp nx targets and requirements-dev.txt.

The diff includes unrelated French translation additions in a dev-tooling change and drops the file's trailing newline. The fr.json hunks add insufficientData, saving, error/success, totalDuration, minutes, none, emptyState, unknownMerchant and andMore keys (already present in en.json and ro.json), and end with `\ No newline at end of file`. Separately, devcontainer.json's new postStartCommand runs `npm run generate 2>/dev/null || true` on every container start. That may regenerate tracked files like these, and any failure is hidden.

The fix overwrites the stored original value of every property with AfterSaveBehavior.Throw (primary keys and any property the user configured as read-only after save) whenever an entry is set to Modified, so a change the user made to a read-only property is now silently thrown away instead of raising PropertyReadOnlyAfterSave. Trigger: for an entity tracked as Unchanged, `var entry = ctx.Entry(e); e.ReadOnlyProp = "x"; entry.State = EntityState.Modified; ctx.SaveChanges();`. The `EntityEntry.State` setter (EntityEntry.cs:78-87) calls `InternalEntry.SetEntityState(value)` directly and does not run DetectChanges. SetEntityState now runs `SetOriginalValue(property, this[property], skipChangeDetection: true)` for every Throw property (lines 287-292), so the original snapshot becomes "x". DetectChanges in SaveChanges then finds no difference, the property is never flagged Modified, and the guard at InternalEntryBase.cs:1655-1661 (`GetAfterSaveBehavior() == Throw && IsModified(property)` throws PropertyReadOnlyAfterSave) never fires. The update is dropped without any error. `entry.OriginalValues` also now reports the new value, which misleads auditing code and interceptors. No other check takes over the guard's job on this path.

The change treats the symptom (a bad original-value snapshot for complex-type shadow properties) with a broad rewrite of original values for all Throw properties on all entity types, rather than fixing how the snapshot is built for the complex-type discriminator. The added comment names the cause itself: "for shadow properties on complex types whose snapshot stores default values". But the condition `afterSaveBehavior == PropertySaveBehavior.Throw && property.GetOriginalValueIndex() >= 0 && !IsConceptualNull(property)` is not limited to complex types, shadow properties or discriminators. It runs for every Modified transition with modifyProperties, including on ordinary entity keys. That is the source of the regression above.

The new test covers only the disconnected-Update path with one input, and nothing checks that read-only-after-save properties on already-tracked entities still raise an error when changed, so the regression the fix introduces passes the suite. The test builds a fresh `updatedEntity`, calls `context.Update(updatedEntity)` and SaveChanges, then asserts only `reloaded.Id`, `NotNull(reloaded.Prop)` and `False(reloaded.Prop.OptionalValue)`. The diff adds no case where a tracked entity's Throw property is changed and the state is then set to Modified expecting PropertyReadOnlyAfterSave. It also does not assert the discriminator's IsModified flag or original value, which the comment at lines 94-95 says is the behaviour under test.

The change adds work on a path the code marks as hot: a SetOriginalValue call (with its own lookups and snapshot write) for every Throw property, keys included, every time an entity is marked Modified. The loop sits under the existing `// Hot path; do not use LINQ` comment (line 274). It now calls `IsConceptualNull(property)`, `this[property]` and `SetOriginalValue(...)` for every key property of every entity attached or updated as Modified, even where the original already equals the current value.

The change loosens the type of the global `--_fs-base` font-size token from `<length>` to `*`. That affects every `--fs-*` size in the library, and nothing in the Legend work explains why it was needed. An invalid override now breaks every derived font size instead of falling back to 1rem. The diff changes `@property --_fs-base { syntax: "<length>"` to `syntax: "*"`. Every token from `--fs-2xs` to `--fs-6xl` is built as `calc(var(--_fs-base) * pow(...))` (variables.css:76-86). With the `<length>` type, a non-length override such as `--_fs-base: 16` or `large` was rejected and the 1rem initial value was kept. With `*` the value is substituted as written, so the `calc` is invalid wherever it is used. Relative overrides such as `em` are also no longer resolved once at the root; they pass down as unresolved text. No Legend file reads `--_fs-base`.

When an older turn reuses a raw tool-call id that also appears in the latest assistant turn, the older tool call is renamed but its tool result is left alone, so the older call/result pair no longer matches and the provider may reject the request. Older assistant messages always go through rewriteAssistantToolCallIds (only `index === latestAssistantIndex` is skipped, line 270). But a toolResult anywhere in the transcript is skipped whenever `preservedLatestToolCallIds.has(toolResultId)` (line 286), so an older toolResult is skipped too, not just the latest turn's. Older assistant id `call_1` becomes `call1`, while the older toolResult keeps `toolCallId: "call_1"`.

The latest turn's preserved ids are never put in the `used` set, so a rewritten older id can come out identical to a preserved latest id, leaving duplicate tool-call ids in the transcript. `resolve` calls makeUniqueToolId({ id, used, mode }), and makeUniqueToolId dedupes only against `used`. The preserve block (lines 244-261) adds the latest ids only to `preservedLatestToolCallIds`, not to `used` or `map`. For example, in strict mode an older id `a_b` sanitizes to `ab`, and a preserved latest id `ab` is then a duplicate. This undoes the collision guarantee the function's comment promises ("de-duping via suffix").

Session-history sanitization now sends the latest assistant turn's tool-call ids unsanitized to Copilot Claude, even when that turn came from a different provider earlier in the session, so ids in a format Copilot rejects (e.g. containing `|` or `:`) may now reach the request. resolveTranscriptPolicy sets `sanitizeToolCallIds` to true for Copilot Claude (the anthropic/openai-completions branch) and also sets `preserveLatestAssistantTurn = isCopilotClaude`. sanitizeSessionHistory passes both to sanitizeSessionMessagesImages, which now skips rewriting the latest assistant message whatever model produced it. Nothing checks isValidCloudCodeAssistToolId before preserving the ids. sanitizeSessionHistory also reads a model snapshot (`modelChanged`), so a session can switch providers mid-way.

The rule for picking the 'latest assistant turn' differs from dropThinkingBlocks, so the two passes can preserve different messages and break the doc's promise that one latest turn is kept verbatim. tool-call-id.ts takes any message with `role === "assistant"` (line 250). thinking.ts dropThinkingBlocks uses isAssistantMessageWithContent, which also requires `Array.isArray(message.content)`. If the last assistant message has string content, tool-call-id preserves it and rewrites the earlier tool-calling assistant turn, while dropThinkingBlocks preserves that earlier turn.

The diff adds a new branch to tool-call-id sanitization with no test: nothing covers the latest assistant turn and its paired results keeping their ids while older turns are rewritten, or the collision and id-reuse cases. The diff changes only docs, images.ts, google.ts, attempt.ts and tool-call-id.ts. Searching for `preserveLatestAssistantTurn` turns up tests only in thinking.test.ts and transcript-policy.test.ts. No test calls sanitizeToolCallIdsForCloudCodeAssist with the new options argument.

The new doc line says the latest turn's paired tool-result ids are preserved "so replayed tool calls stay matched", but the code also skips older tool results with the same raw id and does not reserve preserved ids against collisions, so the matching guarantee does not hold in general. See tool-call-id.ts lines 286 (the membership check applies to every toolResult in the transcript) and 242-261 (preserved ids are never added to `used`).

If the runtime config is malformed or truncated, the new Node probe may print a fragment of the file's raw contents, which may include credential material, into the CI log through stderr. The jq it replaced did not echo file contents when it failed to parse. The new line runs `JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("/home/node/.openclaw/.runtime-openclaw.json","utf8"))` with no try/catch. In recent Node versions (Check 10 says the container runs Node 22), the SyntaxError from a bad parse quotes the input near the failure point (`Unexpected token 'x', "..." is not valid JSON`). The uncaught exception goes to stderr. `gce_ssh_lastline` captures only stdout (`gce_ssh "$1" | tail -1`), so stderr goes straight into the workflow log. The old `jq -cer ... /home/node/.openclaw/.runtime-openclaw.json` reported only line and column on a parse error. Whether this file holds inline secrets isn't shown in the repo: nothing in the export writes `.runtime-openclaw.json`. The trigger is a corrupt or partly written file at verify time, so this is an unusual path. A fix is to wrap the parse in try/catch, print a fixed message and call `process.exit(1)`.

The new probe crams about 600 characters of JavaScript into one escaped line, even though the same file already has a readable pattern for remote Node probes. That makes it hard to review and easy to break. Check 8 (lines 239-390) keeps its script in a heredoc (`browser_probe_js="$(cat <<'NODE' ... NODE)"`), escapes it with `printf '%q'` and runs it with `node --input-type=module -e ${browser_probe_js_escaped}`. Line 152 instead embeds the whole script inline in `bash -lc 'node -e '\''const fs=require(\"node:fs\");...'\'''`, with escaped quotes at every level.

The jq-to-Node rewrite of the staging credential-route probe has no test and no stated reason, so whether it behaves the same as before is unverified. A quoting mistake would only show up as a failed staging deploy. diff.patch changes only this one line in scripts/verify.sh and adds no tests. acceptance.md points to story.md and tests.lock, but neither is in the packet. The repo has no test that runs scripts/verify.sh: grep finds it only in .github/workflows/verify.yml, docs and other scripts. The probe goes through three levels of quoting (local double quotes, the remote shell, then `bash -lc '...'`), and nothing runs it against a sample config. From reading it, the logic matches the old jq: null and array routes and a missing or empty mode all exit 1, and a non-string credentialsFile becomes null.

A node that has annotations but no compartments is drawn with its stereotype text on top of the class name, because layout reserves no header space for annotations unless compartments exist. SizeStandardNode only branches to SizeClassNode when `node.Compartments.Count > 0` (DefaultLayoutEngine.cs:436), so an annotation-only node gets standard sizing and no `label:centerY`. The label is then centred at `node.Height / 2` (SvgNodeWriter.cs:146). But the renderer still calls AppendClassCompartments when `node.Annotations.Count > 0` (line 151), which draws the first annotation at `pad + fontSize * 0.85` (line 318). With a min-height box, that is roughly the same baseline as the centred label, so the two overlap.

A compartment entry whose Label has more than one line overlaps the next entry and can spill past the bottom of the node, because both layout and renderer reserve only one line per entry. Layout sums `(l.FontSize ?? fontSize) * DefaultLabelLineHeight` once per Label (DefaultLayoutEngine.cs:508). The renderer writes every line from `GetRenderedLabelLines(line)` and advances `lineBaseline` for each (lines 353-357), but moves `currentY` by only one line height per Label (line 358). So the next entry starts on top of the second rendered line, and the node height does not cover the extra lines.

Header height ignores each annotation's own font size and line count, so a large-font or multi-line stereotype overlaps the class name rendered below it. `annotationsHeight = node.Annotations.Count * fontSize * DefaultLabelLineHeight` uses the class label's font size and counts one line per annotation, and `label:centerY` is derived from it (line 498). The renderer advances `annBaseline += annFontSize * DefaultLabelLineHeight` for every rendered line of every annotation (SvgNodeWriter.cs:321-326), so its annotation block can be taller than the space layout reserved.

Compartment and annotation text is never wrapped to LayoutHints.MaxNodeWidth, so class nodes can grow wider than the configured maximum, while the class name is wrapped to it. PrepareNodeLabels only calls PrepareLabelLines on `node.Label` (lines 327-331), which applies `hints.MaxNodeWidth`. SizeClassNode takes `maxTextWidth` from the unwrapped compartment lines and annotations (lines 473-485) and sets `node.Width = Math.Max(minWidth, maxTextWidth + 2 * pad)` with no MaxNodeWidth cap.

The new rendering path (dividers, annotation and compartment text, colour escaping) has no tests; only layout sizing is tested. The diff adds AppendClassCompartments and changes how AppendNode resolves the text colour. The only new test file is tests/DiagramForge.Tests/Layout/ClassDiagramLayoutTests.cs, which asserts only on Width, Height, X, Y and Metadata. No test renders SVG for a node with Compartments or Annotations, so the overlap defects above go uncaught.

ClassNode_Width_AnnotationContributesToWidth passes even if annotations are ignored in width sizing, so it does not test what its name claims. The test asserts `diagramWithAnn.Nodes["C"].Width >= diagramNoAnn.Nodes["C2"].Width`. Both nodes have the same name and compartment, so with annotations ignored the widths are equal and `>=` still holds. Similarly, ClassNode_Width_DrivenByWidestCompartmentLine only checks `node > minW`, not that the width covers the line.

Header and compartment geometry is duplicated between layout and renderer, and the renderer's fallback header height disagrees with layout, which invites drift. The renderer repeats `compPad = pad / 2` and the per-line advance that SizeClassNode uses. Its fallback, used when `class:headerHeight` is missing, is `pad + (node.Label.FontSize ?? fontSize) + pad`. That fallback leaves out the annotation height and the multi-line label height that SizeClassNode includes (DefaultLayoutEngine.cs:495). `(node.Label.FontSize ?? fontSize)` is also redundant, because `fontSize` already equals that expression.

TraceEvent is a #[repr(C)] enum, so its variants carry internal padding and the shorter variants leave the union tail uninitialised. sys_ktrace reinterprets whole entries as bytes and copies them to userspace, which can leak kernel stack bytes to any process (and reading padding as u8 is undefined behaviour). A repr(C) enum is laid out as a tag plus a union of the variant structs. Dispatch{u32,u8,u64} has 3 padding bytes after `core`, YieldNow{u32,u8} leaves about 19 union bytes unset, and there are 4 bytes of padding between the tag and the 8-aligned union. Only TraceEntry::_pad is zeroed explicitly. trace_event builds each event on the kernel stack and pushes it by value. sys_ktrace then does `core::slice::from_raw_parts(tmp.as_ptr() as *const u8, write_count * entry_size)` followed by copy_to_user (syscall.rs:12475). The comment there, 'raw byte reinterpretation is safe — no uninit bytes', is false. Trigger: a user process calls ktrace(0, buf) after a YieldNow/RunQueueEnqueue entry has been recorded.

sys_ktrace has no privilege check. Any unprivileged process can read every core's trace ring, which holds kernel stack pointers and the user RIP/RSP and PIDs of other users' processes. sys_ktrace checks only core_id < core_count(), buf_ptr != 0 and buf_len before copying. It never calls current_process_ids()/euid, although the kernel has a uid model (procfs.rs:155-158 filters by caller_euid). The ring stores Dispatch.rsp and SwitchOut.saved_rsp (kernel task stack addresses from scheduler run()) and ForkCtxPublish/ForkTrampolineExit rip/rsp for every process.

sys_ktrace always returns the oldest (at most 64) entries and takes no offset, so the newest 192 entries of a full 256-entry ring can never be read, despite the comment saying callers can call again. `const MAX_BATCH: usize = 64; let batch = max_entries.min(MAX_BATCH); ... copy_into(&mut tmp[..batch])`. copy_into always starts at the oldest entry (`start = if self.count < N { 0 } else { self.write_idx }`). The comment reads 'callers can call again for more', but repeated calls return the same oldest slice.

The crash dump prints each core's ring as a separate block rather than one timeline merged and sorted by tick, so the task list's F.1 acceptance criterion is not met. dump_trace_rings loops `for core_id in 0..core_count` and calls for_each_chronological per core, with no merge. The task doc F.1 requires 'Merges all entries into a single timeline sorted by `tick`'. A heap-free k-way merge over per-core indices would satisfy both the no-allocation goal and the criterion.

The userspace wrapper does not match the G.2 criterion and gives callers no way to decode results: it takes raw bytes, returns a raw u64 that mixes counts, u64::MAX and -ENOSYS, and no TraceEntry type is mirrored for userspace. The wrapper is `pub fn ktrace(core_id: u32, buf: &mut [u8]) -> u64`. The task doc G.2 requires `ktrace(core_id: u32, buf: &mut [TraceEntry]) -> Result<usize, ()>` and '`TraceEntry` type re-exported or mirrored in syscall-lib'. The diff adds no TraceEntry to syscall-lib.

The feature-gate track is only partly implemented: kernel-core has no `trace` feature, the kernel feature does not forward to it, and xtask has no trace-off build or check. The 'xtask check passes with trace on and off' criterion is unverified by any script. The diff adds only `[features] default = ["trace"] trace = []` to kernel/Cargo.toml. Task doc H.1 requires a `trace` feature in kernel-core/Cargo.toml with trace_ring.rs gated. H.2 requires the kernel feature to enable `kernel-core/trace`. H.3 requires an xtask `--no-trace`/release path. xtask/src/main.rs is unchanged, and lib.rs adds `pub mod trace_ring;` ungated.

Every ring-3 page fault or GPF that kills a user process now prints the full trace ring of every core over serial from inside the exception handler. A process that segfaults repeatedly can stall cores for long periods. `crate::trace::dump_trace_rings();` is added on the user-fault kill paths at lines 453 and 528, before the FAULT_KILL_PID redirect. Each dump prints up to 256 lines per core via _panic_print. At serial speeds that is roughly 20 KB per core per fault, emitted while the exception handler runs.

core_id is truncated to u8 before validation, so out-of-range values such as 256 silently read core 0 instead of returning the documented u64::MAX error. `let core_id = core_id as u8; if core_id >= crate::smp::core_count() { return u64::MAX; }` drops the high bits before the bounds check.

The new docs contradict the implementation and each other, which will mislead readers of crash dumps. docs/43b-kernel-trace-ring.md:136 says 'Events appear in chronological order across all cores' and :155 says 'prints the merged timeline', but lines 111-113 and trace.rs print per core. docs/roadmap/43b-kernel-trace-ring.md says 'merges all per-core rings into a sorted timeline' in both the Milestone Goal and the Crash Auto-Dump sections and cites '15 instrumentation sites', while its outline lists 6+4+7=17. The tasks doc is marked Complete with every acceptance checkbox still unchecked, and its A.1 'atomic write index' is not what was built.

No test covers the I.3 end-to-end requirement (forced panic shows the dump with at least 5 events), the B.2 size bound, the sys_ktrace byte ABI, or copy_into on a partially filled ring. The diff's only tests are host unit tests in trace_ring.rs (snapshot ordering, for_each, and one copy_into on a wrapped ring). There is no QEMU/xtask test of the panic dump, no `size_of::<TraceEntry>() <= 64` assertion, and no test that the bytes sys_ktrace copies are fully initialised.

The public host-function signature types `ctx.hostContext` as optional and possibly undefined, but the runtime always sets it. Extension authors have to cast or null-check to use the new bag, which works against the 'defaults to {}' guarantee. `CallableFn` receives `ctx: RuntimeContextLike`, which declares `readonly hostContext?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined`, while `RuntimeContext` declares `readonly hostContext: Record<string, unknown>` (types/runtime.ts:174). Every new test has to write `(ctx as RuntimeContext).hostContext` to reach it without a null check (host-context.test.ts lines 55, 85, 113, 138, 170).

The host integration docs describe `ctx.metadata` for host functions but never mention the new `hostContext` option or field, so hosts and extension authors have no documentation for the feature. A grep for `hostContext` under docs/ returns nothing. integration-host.md:257-288 lists the `ctx` contents as 'variables, pipeValue, and session metadata' and documents only `ctx.metadata`. The change edits only CHANGELOG.md and source files.

Adding `hostContext` as a required member of the exported `RuntimeContext` interface breaks type-checking for any downstream code that builds a `RuntimeContext` object literal. The CHANGELOG lists the change only under 'Added'. `readonly hostContext: Record<string, unknown>;` has no `?`, unlike the neighbouring `metadata?`. Inside this repo, the only literal builder, `assertType`'s `minimalContext` (eval/index.ts:89-119), had to be patched to add `hostContext: {}`. `RuntimeContext` is exported from '@rcrsr/rill', as the test import shows.

The host's `hostContext` object is passed by reference and is not frozen, so any extension or host function can add, replace or delete entries. Those changes are seen by every other extension in the run and by the host's original object. The change does not document this sharing. `hostContext: options.hostContext ?? {}` stores the caller's object as-is, and `createChildContext` copies the same reference (`hostContext: parent.hostContext`). The test 'child context shares same hostContext reference as parent' asserts `refs[0]` is `sharedContext`. The type is `Record<string, unknown>`; the `readonly` applies only to the property, not to the object's contents.

The word search control is never built when the top-words list is empty, so a user whose notes have no repeated word of 5+ characters cannot search for specific words at all, even though the notes contain words to search. buildWordsTab: `if (topWords.getWords().isEmpty()) { wordSearchForm.add(new LabelField("(no data)")); return wordSearchForm; }` comes before the "Word search" header, the ShortTextField and the ButtonField. The top list is empty whenever every word of length >= MIN_WORD_LENGTH occurs once (findWords prunes counts < MIN_PHRASE_FREQUENCY), but the specific-word search counts short and single-occurrence words, so it would still return results.

A search with more than 25 distinct words silently drops the least frequent ones, and the 'combined occurrences' total is understated, because the input limit in the help text is never enforced. WordSearchThread calls `StatisticsUtil.findWords(notesToSearch, searchWords, StatisticsUtil.TOP_N_WORDS)`, and findWords applies `.limit(N)` with N = 25. StatisticsDialog only says "Enter a comma-separated list of 1-25 words" (line 379). WordSearchAction checks only isFormValid (non-blank) and never checks wordSet.size(). showWordSearchResults then sums only the truncated list: `foundWords.getWords().stream().mapToInt(Word::occurrenceCount).sum()`.

Search terms are matched against normalized note text without being normalized themselves, so a term in a different form (uppercase, trailing punctuation, an internal space, or an apostrophe TagList may change) may never match and is reported as zero occurrences. findWords applies normalizeText to the note text but compares tokens with `specificWords.contains(word)` against the raw set. In the UI that set comes from `TagList.fromRawString(...)` / `tag.getTag()`. TagList is an external Snotes class, and nothing in this repo shows that its normalization matches normalizeText (lowercase, keep apostrophes, non-alphanumerics become spaces). A direct caller passing Set.of("Hello") gets no match.

Words with equal counts are ranked in HashMap iteration order, so which words make the top 25 at a tie boundary is arbitrary. This is unlike PhraseList, which has a documented tiebreaker. `.sorted((w1, w2) -> Integer.compare(w2.occurrenceCount(), w1.occurrenceCount()))` followed by `.limit(N)` has no secondary key, and it runs on `wordCounts.entrySet()` of a HashMap.

Every distinct token is kept in a second HashSet for the unique-word count, which undercuts the memory concern the prune comment cites. The work is also wasted on the specific-word search path, where the dialog never shows the count. `uniqueWords.add(word)` runs for every token before any filtering, so the set holds every distinct word. The later comment justifies pruning by the risk of OutOfMemory on large datasets. showWordSearchResults never reads getUniqueWordCount().

Several new tests check only the shape of the output, so they would pass on a broken implementation, for example one that returns an empty list. findWords_shouldLimitResultsToN asserts only `result.getWords().size() <= 3`, which an empty result satisfies. findWords_withNullNoteText_shouldBeIgnored asserts only `assertFalse(result.getWords().isEmpty())`, without checking the words or counts. No test covers the >N specific-words case, WordSearchThread, Word/WordList validation, or the new Phrase wordCount check.

The change tightens the public Phrase record's contract, which the word-statistics feature did not need: it now rejects wordCount 0 and occurrenceCount 0, which the old Javadoc explicitly allowed. The old docs said wordCount was "zero if the phrase is empty" and occurrenceCount "A non-negative integer". The new code throws IllegalArgumentException on `wordCount <= 0` and `occurrenceCount <= 0`. The in-repo callers (findPhrases uses len >= 2 and count >= 2; PhraseListTest uses counts >= 1) still comply, but any external caller that builds a zero-count Phrase now throws.

The architecture doc still says the loader runs 6 parallel worker tasks, but the change adds a seventh. The unchanged context line reads "Loader runs **6 parallel worker tasks** via `ExecutorService`: general counts, per-year, all-months, per-year+month, day-of-week, and phrase extraction", while StatisticsLoaderThread.run now does `workers.add(this::loadWords);`, which makes 7.

Word search runs against the notes list captured when the statistics were loaded, so it may give stale counts after the user edits notes. If that list is the live DataManager list, iterating it off the EDT may also race with edits. WordSearchAction builds `new WordSearchThread(stats.getAllNotes(), wordSet)`. Statistics.allNotes is `dataManager.getNotes()` captured in StatisticsLoaderThread.getStatistics(), and StatisticsExtension caches Statistics until an explicit refresh. The repo does not show whether getNotes() returns a copy.

The quasi-independence model is fitted only on observed (positive) cells, so it exactly reproduces any reviewer-author pair where the reviewer reviews only one author or the author is reviewed by only one reviewer. Those pairs get a Pearson residual of 0 and can never be flagged, so the most exclusive reviewer-author concentrations, which are the classic bias pattern, now report "No bias". fitQuasiIndependenceModel builds its support only from cells with count > 0 (`if (count === 0) continue;`) and rescales each reviewer factor with `reviewerFactors[reviewerPosition] *= rowTotal / fittedRowTotal` (line 171). For a reviewer with a single support cell, that forces E_ij = rowTotal = M_ij, and the column step does the same for an author with a single reviewer. Trigger: 50 PRs by alice, each reviewed only by bob, plus any other unrelated pairs. Then E(bob,alice) = 50, `pearsonResidual = (count - fittedCount)/Math.sqrt(fittedCount)` = 0, and `count > fittedCount && pearsonResidual > threshold` is false at every allowed threshold (≥0.5). The removed z-score code would have flagged bob→alice. More generally, flagging is possible only when the support graph has a cycle. No locked test covers an exclusive pair, and docs/statistics.md and the HTML explanation don't disclose this blind spot.

The change rewrites and deletes baseline tests, which acceptance.md calls the locked acceptance tests, in the same change as the code they judge. Behaviour those tests pinned now goes unchecked, and the packet records no reason or approval. acceptance.md: "The baseline's tests are the locked acceptance tests". The diff deletes "produces no false positives with a high threshold", replaces "flags pairs that exceed a low threshold" and both threshold-boundary tests with new fixtures, and rewrites the sort test (diff lines ~261-835). There is no story.md or tests.lock in the packet or export to show that the spec required these edits.

The test "respects the structural-zero self-review diagonal when fitting expected counts" passes for a reason unrelated to the diagonal, so it would not catch a regression in self-review handling. The fixture is bob→alice ×10 and alice→bob ×10, two disconnected single-cell support components. The IPF fit is saturated, so E = M and the residual is 0 whatever the diagonal handling. `expect(result.flaggedPairs).toEqual([])` holds trivially.

The non-convergence and error-path tests force failure by globally mocking Math.abs and Math.sqrt. That ties them to internal implementation details, so a harmless refactor (for example, dropping Math.abs from the margin check) would break them or make them vacuous. `vi.spyOn(Math, "abs").mockReturnValue(1)` (lines 98 and 290) and `vi.spyOn(Math, "sqrt").mockImplementation(() => { throw "sqrt failed"; })` (line 318). The tests never build a matrix that genuinely fails to converge.

The report explanation implies that only activity-explained pairs escape flagging. In fact, exclusive pairs can never be flagged, so readers may over-trust a "No reviewer-author pair exceeds the configured activity-adjusted bias threshold" result. The text reads "The model matches each reviewer's total outgoing reviews and each author's total incoming reviews, so high-volume people are not flagged merely for being active." docs/statistics.md:112 likewise omits that pairs where the reviewer has a single author, or the author a single reviewer, are fitted exactly.

The `bias-detected` output returns "false" both when no pair is flagged and when the model failed to fit, so a workflow that gates on this output cannot tell "no bias" from "not computed". src/main.ts only logs `logger.warning(`Bias warnings unavailable: ...`)` when modelFitError is set. docs/outputs.md now states that a "false" value does not distinguish the two states, and no separate output exposes modelFitError.

The change rewrites all five component test classes, which the packet says are locked acceptance tests. Nothing in the packet (there is no story.md) records why, so the judging tests were changed by the same change they judge, and some of their assertions were weakened. acceptance.md: "The baseline's tests are the locked acceptance tests; tests.lock lists them." The diff edits BasicTest, CallbackTest, LifecycleTest, MiscTest and ReconnectTest. It replaces assertions such as `assertTrue(disconnectCalled.await(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS), "onDisconnect must fire even when onTransportDrop throws")` with a bare `disconnectCalled.await()`, removes the `"onTransportRestore must fire after successful reconnect"` assertion message, and drops the onDisconnect hook from `throwing onTransportDrop in reconnect loop does not abort reconnect`.

The 5-second limit on waiting for a callback is gone. If a callback stops firing, the test now hangs until runTest's own wall-clock timeout and fails with a generic timeout instead of a named assertion, so the suite gets slower and the failure is harder to diagnose. `CountDownLatch.await(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)` inside `assertTrue(...)` was replaced by `CompletableDeferred.await()` with no `withTimeout`, here and in BasicTest:91-92, CallbackTest:68/193/196/243/244/294/326/379 and LifecycleTest:121. gradle/libs.versions.toml pins kotlinx-coroutines 1.10.2, where runTest's default timeout is 60 s.

The constructor parameter `testScheduler` does nothing useful, and its name shadows TestScope.testScheduler inside every runTest block. The tests only work because the two happen to be the same object, which will mislead whoever maintains this next. Every subclass passes a fresh `ComponentTestBase(TestCoroutineScheduler())`. The test bodies call `runTest(StandardTestDispatcher(testScheduler)) { ... testScheduler.advanceTimeBy(...) }`, and inside that lambda `testScheduler` resolves to the TestScope receiver's property, not the base-class field. `waitUntil` and `tearDown` use the base-class field.

The CHANGELOG still describes the old `waitUntil` helpers, which this change replaced, and has no entry for the test refactor. CHANGELOG.md:14 says "`waitUntil` helpers gain a synchronous fast-path (`if (condition()) return`) that avoids releasing the test coroutine to `workRunner`". The new `ComponentTestBase.waitUntil` (line 48) is a single synchronous loop that calls `testScheduler.advanceTimeBy(10)` up to 500 times, with no Dispatchers.Default or withTimeout path.

The 'Percentile' column is really a lamb's linear position between the breed minimum and maximum, not a percentile, so phrases like '32nd — well below average' can mislead the reader. Every value matches (EBV - min)/(max - min). For example, sire BWT (-0.225+0.944)/2.244 = 0.32 is shown as "32nd", and dam WWT (2.72+3.019)/9.209 = 0.62 is shown as "62nd". This copies the earlier reports' convention, but the column header and notes call it a percentile.

The change has no stated acceptance criteria or test that checks the report's figures, so the arithmetic and wording errors above could pass the gate unnoticed. acceptance.md says only "story.md is the spec. The baseline's tests are the locked acceptance tests". The export contains no story.md and no tests, and the diff adds a single markdown file with nothing checking its numbers against NSIP data.
